title: Sets and multisets
key_idea: A **multiset** is a set where elements may repeat; a $k$-element multiset from an $n$-element set is counted by the multiset coefficient $\binom{n+k-1}{k}$ (stars and bars). The binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ counts $k$-element subsets; both have generating function identities that are the main workhorses of elementary enumeration.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Key formulas: $\binom{n}{k} = n!/(k!(n-k)!)$, the multinomial theorem, stars-and-bars $\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, the Vandermonde identity, and generating functions $(1+x)^n = \sum_k \binom{n}{k} x^k$ and $1/(1-x)^n = \sum_k \binom{n+k-1}{k} x^k$.

notation.description: Multinomial coefficient $n!/(k_1!\cdots k_r!)$ where $\sum k_i = n$
